_comment: DUM-E approvable actions. DUM-E can only PROPOSE these; the owner approves and runs them with `dume approve <id>`. Every entry MUST declare `deletes` (list, or the string 'none') and a `class`: mutates | housekeeping | permanent_delete. The loader refuses the file if either is missing (Deletion Mandate M4).

llama_start.summary: Start the AI brain (llama-server on :8081, model chosen by the start script, default default quant).
warnings: Uses most of the GPU memory. The VRAM watchdog may pause it again if VRAM runs low.
Unloads any Ollama model from the GPU first (LLAMA_OFFLOAD_OLLAMA=1).

llama_stop.summary: Stop the AI brain. Jarvis, Virtual Self and the Personal Feed lose their model; DUM-E chat stops working until it is started again.
warnings: This ends the current DUM-E conversation's model.

llama_restart.summary: Restart the AI brain (stop, then start).
warnings: Interrupts every client of :8081 for a minute or two.

ollama_unload.summary: Unload every Ollama model from GPU memory (keep_alive 0). Models stay on disk.

service_start.summary: Start one Homelab service through Homelab Control (fortress start <id>).
warnings: GPU services pass through Homelab Control's GPU guard, which may refuse.
Not offered for immich (must be started with its --env-file, see manual 21) or mediastack (its data disk /mnt/movie-storage is not mounted; downloads would land on the full root disk, see manual 22).
Not offered for virtual_self_archive (Homelab Control ignores compose profiles, so it would act on the main Virtual Self stack) or vitalis (never deployed). See manuals 35 and 37.

service_stop.summary: Stop one Homelab service through Homelab Control (fortress stop <id>; compose services use 'docker compose stop', which keeps containers and data).
warnings: Not offered for virtual_self_archive: Homelab Control ignores compose profiles and would stop the whole Virtual Self stack.

watchdog_restart.summary: Restart the VRAM watchdog (fortress stop vram_watchdog, then fortress start vram_watchdog).
warnings: If the AI is paused and the GPU is quiet, the watchdog resumes the AI within about a minute.

watchdog_clear_pause.summary: Remove the watchdog's pause flag and start the AI brain now, overriding the watchdog's wait.
warnings: Overrides the VRAM safety pause. If the GPU is busy, the AI may run out of memory or be paused again.

backup_run_daily.summary: Run the daily off-site backup now, the same way cron does (vault-backup/scripts/cron-daily.sh: takes the backup lock, skips if another backup holds it, logs to cron-daily.log, reports failures as incidents).
deletes: old restic snapshots beyond keep-daily 14 / keep-weekly 8 / keep-monthly 12 (restic forget --prune, PERMANENT)
temporary work and plaintext files the backup creates for itself
warnings: Skips immediately if another backup holds /mnt/backup-volume/vault-backup/run.lock (on 2026-10-29 the photos bootstrap upload had held it for weeks).
Output goes to /mnt/backup-volume/vault-backup/logs/cron-daily.log (DUM-E: log_tail log=vault_cron_daily). This terminal stays busy until the run ends; it can take hours.
Retention runs after a successful backup: restic forget --prune deletes older snapshots permanently.

docker_image_cleanup_run.summary: Run the weekly Docker image cleanup now: the same script cron runs on Sundays 07:30 (homelab/control/docker-image-cleanup.py --apply). IMAGES ONLY, volumes are never touched. Always show the owner image_cleanup_preview first.
deletes: Docker images that no container uses (cine-immich images and anything in docker-image-cleanup.keep are skipped)

Stopped containers of registered Homelab stacks that have been stopped 7+ days, whose image can be pulled again and that hold no files of their own (removed WITHOUT their volumes; cine-immich skipped)
warnings: Volumes are never deleted: the script cannot issue a volume command, and the docker guard refuses them too.

Locally built images that nothing uses (for example virtual-self-memory rollback tags) are removed and cannot be pulled back. The owner protects one by adding its name to homelab/control/docker-image-cleanup.keep.
A removed stack's image is pulled or rebuilt again the next time that stack is started.
